title: Amitabh Bachchan Dismisses Retirement Talk After Late-Night Blog Sparks Frenzy
excerpt: The 83-year-old described hosting KBC 18 as a 'heart-breaking experience' before signing off with 'I wish to retire now' — a line that set off a frenzy he later brushed aside.
body:
• Amitabh Bachchan ended a late-night blog entry on September 7 with the words "I wish to retire now .. it is late .. and the night invites," setting off speculation that he was quitting Kaun Banega Crorepati.
  • The 83-year-old said he was describing emotionally draining days hosting KBC's 18th season — and meant retiring to bed, not retiring from television.
  • His clarification, carried in follow-up reports, has reassured fans that he is stepping away from neither Bollywood nor the quiz show.

Amitabh Bachchan has dismissed a fresh wave of retirement speculation triggered by his own late-night blog post, telling fans he has no plans to step away from Kaun Banega Crorepati or from films. The 83-year-old actor wrote the entry at 2:59 am on September 7 from his Mumbai home, Jalsa, describing hosting KBC's 18th season as a "heart-breaking experience" — and signed off with a line that went viral within hours.

"I wish to retire now .. it is late .. and the night invites."

— Amitabh Bachchan, in his blog

"Some contestants come with such grave personal stories, that it becomes difficult to contain not just our feelings for them but also to continue hosting the show," he wrote, according to Glamsham. He added that he would not describe the incidents further because it would take away from what the episodes themselves should reveal, before the abrupt sign-off that fans and media outlets alike read as a possible farewell.

Context & Background

Bachchan has hosted Kaun Banega Crorepati on Sony Entertainment Television since its debut in 2000 — every season except the third — and is currently fronting its 18th season, which premiered on August 10 at 9 pm and also streams on Sony LIV. The show is built on the real stories of ordinary contestants, and Bachchan's blog has long been a window into how much those encounters stay with him.

A few days before the viral post, in an entry labelled DAY 6764, he had described a very different encounter — a "heart warming experience" with a young woman who had taken responsibility for her family's financial difficulties and gone on to win on the show. "The girl is the biggest asset of the family," he wrote, in a passage urging education and empowerment of daughters. The contrast between the two entries, days apart, shows how deeply the contestants' stories affect the host, according to SantaBanta.

The demanding schedule has been public. In August, Bachchan revealed he had worked a continuous 24-hour shift for KBC 18, writing that "the importance of its presentation and its timely work was necessary," and joking that missing the announced broadcast date "would mean a job replacement for me," according to NewKerala. His late-night blogging habit — often past 2 am — is well known to his millions of followers.

Impact & Analysis

The episode says as much about audience anxiety as it does about the actor's plans. Every cryptic post from Bachchan is now parsed as a possible career signal, and a single word — "retire" — was enough to start the rumour mill. Bachchan's response, as reported by the Hindustan Times, was characteristically wry: in English, he said, "retire" simply means going to bed.

That reading is consistent with his own history. He has repeatedly used the word in his blog to mean turning in for the night after long shoots. The substance of the September 7 post was not about quitting at all — it was about the emotional weight of sitting across from people carrying grief, illness and economic distress, and finding it hard to hold his composure.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, Bachchan remains a rare cultural constant — and KBC is one of the few shows that families abroad watch in lockstep with relatives back home, streaming episodes on Sony LIV from the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf. Rumours of his exit travel fast in diaspora group chats precisely because the show is a shared ritual, and his reassurance lands with an audience that has grown up with him over five decades.

What's Next

KBC's 18th season continues its nightly run on Sony Entertainment Television and Sony LIV, and there has been no announcement from the channel or from Bachchan about any change in hosting. If the blog is any indication, the most likely future is more of the same: late-night entries, gruelling shoots, and an 83-year-old host who keeps showing up.
